correctness.rationale: An exact weighted-path definition and run-boundary enumeration prove the family for each a>=5. originality.rationale: The new object is the conditional stochastic-tail order of the two-sided KS statistic as the total run count varies, including a sharp finite minimal failure and infinitely many analytic counterexamples. Inspected modern primary texts develop joint enumeration or other run statistics but do not state or logically imply the specific conditional sign classification on the material inspected. General classical joint-distribution formulas might enable derivation and are a residual priority risk; no claim of bibliographic uniqueness is made.

value.rationale: The null relationship of two classical two-sample tests is a motivated issue: larger alternation count may intuitively accompany smaller empirical CDF discrepancy. The first precise failure and a nonisolated infinite family disprove a natural full stochastic-order expectation at a sharp small-sample boundary; an analytic sign mechanism supplements exhaustive finite work. The finding is not a routine moment computation or an arbitrary slice.
